title: Korean Demilitarized Zone
summary: The Korean Demilitarized Zone is a buffer strip about 4 km wide and roughly 250 km long across the Korean Peninsula, created by the armistice that took effect on 27 July 1953. A fence marks the Military Demarcation Line at its centre. Decades without farming or development turned it into an unplanned wildlife refuge.

uncertainty.note: Start is the armistice date of 27 July 1953; the zone still exists, so the end is the present. South Korea did not sign, and no peace treaty followed.

where.modern_name: Korean Demilitarized Zone, between North and South Korea
where.historical_name: Armistice buffer zone along the 38th parallel, set up by the 1953 armistice between the UN Command and the North Korean and Chinese commands

importance.justification: The most heavily militarised frontier in the world, still the line dividing the Koreas, with an unintended wildlife refuge.

related.because: The armistice terms required both sides to pull back, which created the buffer zone.
The zone follows the front line where the Korean War stopped.

audience_note: Concerns an unresolved military confrontation; the zone remains heavily armed.
reviewer_note: Length figures differ: NASA 250 km, EBSCO 258 km (160 miles); the summary says roughly 250 km. "Most heavily militarised" in the importance text is not from an opened source. The pin is Wikidata's centre; the zone is a line, not a point.
